description: Disabilities Awareness builds understanding and respect: disability etiquette and terms, visiting an agency, meeting people with disabilities, accessibility and accommodation, outreach, a personal commitment, and careers serving people with disabilities.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Terms and etiquette
requirements.summary: Disability terms such as accessibility, accommodation and person-first language, and why etiquette matters.

requirements.title: Visiting an agency
requirements.summary: Visiting an agency that works with people with disabilities and learning about its work.

requirements.title: Learning from others
requirements.summary: Two options, such as talking with a person with a disability, an adaptive sport, independent-living aids or an awareness activity.

requirements.title: Accessibility or accommodation
requirements.summary: One option: surveying locations for accessibility, or for accommodations for invisible disabilities.

requirements.title: Outreach
requirements.summary: One option: a presentation, volunteer service, or researching common myths about disability.

requirements.title: Your commitment
requirements.summary: A commitment to a positive attitude toward people with disabilities, and how your awareness has changed.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Professions that serve people with disabilities and the training for one of them.
